{{nihongo|'''Kushitamanomikoto Shrine'''|櫛玉命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Kushitamanomikoto Shrine''' (くしたまのみことじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|Q752397|qid=Q752397}}, {{ill|Takaichi District, Nara|Q1117901|qid=Q1117901}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=major Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank was village shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The following four deities are enshrined<ref name="#1"/>.
*Kushitamahiko-no-Mikoto
*Kushitamahime-no-Mikoto
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Akama-no-Mikoto (Kushiakama-no-Mikoto)}}
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyotama-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
=== Historical outline ===
The founding period is unknown, but one theory says that in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}, Araki no Mikoto, descendant of Kushitamahiko-no-Mikoto (Kushitama-no-Mikoto), was granted thirty generations of land in Kose in recognition of ancestral merit, and the worship of ancestors there was the shrine's beginning. It was once called Tamatsukuri Shrine, but from early {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called {{ill|Hachiman shrine|Q11390939|qid=Q11390939}}, and the deities were changed to {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman Ōkami|qid=Q261637}}. On December 25, {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 23 ({{ill|1890|Q7832|qid=Q7832}}), the shrine name and deities were restored to ancient form.

In Yamato Shiryo, quoting Gokōgun Jinja-ki, it says "the two deities Kushitamahiko and Kushitamahime were also invited from {{ill|Yata ni Imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine|Q11584205|qid=Q11584205}} (Daidō 3)," so the deity may be {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}. However, according to Takaichi District Shrine Chronicle and Nara Prefectural History, which also cite Gokōgun Jinja-ki, the enshrined Kushitamahiko-no-Mikoto is said to be a child of {{ill|Takamimusubi|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto}}<ref>The original Gokōgun Jinja-ki says child of Izanagi-no-Mikoto.</ref> and father of Ame-no-Akama-no-Mikoto, with no mention of invitation from Yata ni imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine. It cannot be ruled out that this is {{ill|Isetsuhiko|Q17193127|qid=Q17193127}}<ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Jingi Zensho II |date=1907-02-12 |publisher=Shibunkaku}}</ref>. However, Gokōgun Jinja-ki also says "there are Yata and Hata villages in Kose-gō," "two shrines, Yatama Shrine and Hatama Shrine," and "the two distant-ancestor deities Kushitamahiko and Kushitamahime were invited from Yata ni imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine and called Yatama-sha," indicating a high possibility that Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mikashikiya-hime}}, Ame-no-Akama-no-Mikoto, and Toyotama-no-Mikoto were worshiped. Confusion may have arisen because Yata ni imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine once enshrined {{ill|Futodama|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, child of Takamimusubi.

Kushitamahime-no-Mikoto is considered consort of Kushitamahiko-no-Mikoto. Also, Kushitama-no-Mikoto worshiped at {{ill|Hirose Taisha|Q705281|qid=Q705281}} is Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto.
